sections.name: File setup, mean
sections.title: Chase loading and mean helper
sections.what: Loads the outcome model and every fixture match that counts as a valid chase. Converts each match's deliveries into game states and builds a win model for each chase. Defines a simple average helper.
sections.why: Gives the tests real chase data and a way to compare averages.
sections.watch_out: Only chases that pass the contract check are used, so a rule change in that check changes the test data.

sections.name: leverage and swing on real chases (leverage)
sections.title: Leverage and swing checks
sections.what: Checks that at least four chases are available. Checks that death-over leverage has a higher average than powerplay leverage. Checks that swing equals the size of the change between two points, lies between 0 and 1, and that leverage is never negative.
sections.why: Likely reason: confirms the measure ranks moments as expected and stays within valid bounds.
sections.watch_out: The ball cut-offs for the powerplay and death overs are fixed in the test. Using different cut-offs changes the answer.

summary: Checks the leverage and swing measures on real chases from committed fixtures. Death overs should matter more than the powerplay, and swing should equal the size of the change in win probability.
purpose: Validates the importance measure that decides which moments are worth asking a fan about.
why: Likely reason: the measure is only useful if it ranks moments the way cricket intuition expects and stays within sensible bounds.
how: Loads the outcome model and every fixture match that passes the contract check. Turns each delivery into a game state, builds a win model for each chase, and checks chase count, average leverage in death overs versus the powerplay, swing bounds, and that leverage is never negative.
inputs: data/models/outcomes-v1.json and the fixture files in data/fixtures/cricsheet.
risks: Adding or removing fixtures changes the averages. The death and powerplay ball cut-offs are fixed in the test, so changing them changes the answer.
debug: Check the chase count first. If death leverage is not above powerplay leverage, check the model values and the state counts for those balls.
